dedupe_keys.name: dhdrift district heating concept drift benchmark

description: DHDrift is a synthetic district heating load data set with documented ground-truth timings of concept drift, for benchmarking drift detection and adaptive load forecasting algorithms. It was published by Kai Derzsi, Jonas Klingebiel and Dirk Müller. It holds 901 hourly heat load time series over four years (2020 to 2023), generated by dynamic building energy simulation of a 32-building residential district in Aachen, Germany. Nine drift scenarios represent realistic operational changes, namely network expansion, building refurbishment and the introduction of night setback control, each at three severity levels with 100 randomised realisations. Supplementary data give 256 individual building load profiles and building attributes for building custom districts. Coverage is one simulated district at hourly resolution. The data are a ZIP of about 568 MB with a README on Zenodo (version 1.0.0, January 2026) under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost. Caveats: loads are simulated, not measured, and represent one residential district and climate. Simulation uses are testing forecasting and monitoring methods for district heating operation and digital twins. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
